market_summary: US tech stocks dominated Monday's session with strong analyst upgrades driving momentum. Microsoft received a Buy upgrade from Melius Research targeting $665, supported by Azure growth expectations exceeding 50% by Q4 FY27, while Wells Fargo raised its target to $725. Nvidia hit fresh all-time highs with $150 billion in new share buyback authorization, and Tesla delivered better-than-expected Q3 vehicles of 486,532 units, nearly quadrupling its Cybercab fleet in Texas. Apple unveiled a Siri AI smart home hub launching October 13, competing directly with Amazon and Google. Alphabet's Gemini 4 Argon model launch disappointed some investors as it arrives months late with limited availability. Broader markets focused on AI monetization challenges and capex sustainability as hyperscalers plan $1.3 trillion in data center investments for 2027.

items.headline: Melius Research upgrades Microsoft to Buy with $665 price target on AI security demand
items.summary: <cite index="6-3,6-4">Melius expects Azure to grow more than 50% by Q4 FY27, with enterprises choosing to spend on secure systems that can route AI models.</cite> <cite index="6-1">Melius raised fiscal 2027 earnings estimates by 2% and fiscal 2028 by 4%.</cite>

items.headline: Wells Fargo raises Microsoft price target to $725 from $700 on AI monetization
items.summary: <cite index="8-5,8-6">The move represents a 3.57% increase in Wells Fargo's target, with analyst Michael Turrin citing Microsoft's AI monetization, November's Ignite conference and new segment reporting.</cite>

items.headline: Apple to unveil Siri AI smart home hub lineup on October 13, 2026
items.summary: <cite index="19-5,19-7">Apple is set to unveil a smart home hub with a screen, an updated HomePod mini, and a new Apple TV at its October 13 event, all powered by Siri AI.</cite> <cite index="10-3,10-4,10-5">The main product is a roughly 6-inch display designed to recognize different household members and serve as a central controller for locks, thermostats, FaceTime, music and connected devices.</cite>

items.headline: Tesla expands Texas Cybercab fleet fourfold to 169 units following Austin commercial launch
items.summary: <cite index="22-3,22-4,22-8,22-10">Tesla nearly quadrupled its Cybercab fleet in Texas from 45 to 169 in a month since the driverless two-seaters launched in Austin on Sept. 3, based on Texas DMV records.</cite> <cite index="22-12,22-13,22-14">Early riders gave it mixed reviews, with some complaining about long waits, pickups in the wrong spot, and problems with butterfly doors and trunk.</cite>

items.headline: Tesla reports Q3 2026 vehicle deliveries of 486,532, beating forecasts by 6.5%
items.summary: <cite index="29-2,29-6">Tesla delivered 486,532 vehicles in Q3 2026, exceeding the 456,896 forecast by Reuters' Visible Alpha by approximately 6.5%.</cite> <cite index="29-8,29-9">FSD subscriptions reached 1.48 million (56% increase YoY), and Tesla added Cybercab to its Texas robotaxi fleet with FSD approved in eight European countries.</cite>

items.headline: Nvidia announces $150 billion increase to share repurchase authorization, total now $235 billion
items.summary: <cite index="34-12">Nvidia's Board authorized an additional $150 billion under the company's share repurchase program, increasing total remaining authorized amount to $235 billion.</cite>

items.headline: Alphabet unveils Gemini 4 Argon AI model after delays, matches rivals on coding and cybersecurity
items.summary: <cite index="49-3,49-4,49-5">Alphabet's new flagship AI model Argon tops the Gemini 4 generation and took months longer than promised. Google says it matches OpenAI's Astra and Anthropic's Opus on key coding and cybersecurity tests, areas where Alphabet had been slipping behind rivals.</cite> <cite index="49-6,49-7">Argon is not available to everyone yet, with Google offering it only to select cybersecurity partners with no public release date announced.</cite>

items.headline: Alphabet projects $195-205 billion data center spending for 2026 amid AI competition
items.summary: <cite index="49-1">Alphabet projects 2026 data center capital spending of $195 billion to $205 billion.</cite> <cite index="49-2">The company is becoming a chip supplier, selling TPUs that Google designs and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing builds.</cite>

items.headline: SGX implements board lot reduction for 11 stocks including three Singapore banks
items.summary: The Singapore Exchange board lot reduction kicks in for 11 stocks including DBS, OCBC and UOB, lowering minimum trade sizes to improve liquidity and accessibility.

items.headline: SGX rolls out youth stock programme to lower barriers for young investors
items.summary: Singapore Exchange and partners launch youth stock programme designed to equip young investors with knowledge and lower participation barriers.

items.headline: Nvidia stock settles at $233.95 with fresh all-time highs driven by AI capex expectations
items.summary: <cite index="30-5,30-14,30-15">Nvidia expects to grow revenue at 70% pace next year, with Q2 guidance revealing the company expects 70% revenue growth during fiscal 2028, making it primed for strong future growth as a $5 trillion company.</cite>

items.headline: AI capex buildup faces revenue monetization test as hyperscalers ramp spending to $1.3 trillion in 2027
items.summary: <cite index="30-16,30-17">AI hyperscalers are expected to ramp up data center spending to nearly $1.3 trillion in 2027 from current estimates, with the big five hyperscalers expected to spend nearly $800 billion on data center build-outs this year.</cite>
